analysis.evidence: The plural imperatives פְּרוּ וּרְבוּ (“be fruitful and multiply”) already identify the addressees. The explicit אַתֶּם at the head of the verse singles out Noah and his sons as the ones receiving the command.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וְ precedes the independent second-person masculine plural pronoun אַתֶּם.

analysis.evidence: In שִׁרְצוּ בָאָרֶץ, the people addressed are to swarm on the earth. The surrounding commands פְּרוּ ‘be fruitful’ and וּרְבוּ ‘multiply’ show that swarming here conveys growing numerous.
analysis.morphology: Qal imperative, second person masculine plural, addressed to וְאַתֶּם. The ending וּ marks the plural.

analysis.evidence: שִׁרְצוּ בָאָרֶץ calls on the addressees to teem on the earth. The next command, וּרְבוּ בָהּ, refers back to the earth as the place where they are to multiply.
analysis.morphology: The preposition בְּ combines with the definite article before א. The noun is singular absolute, common in gender, and takes feminine agreement here in בָהּ.
